reviews.rationale: The proposed necessity is probabilistically qualified, and neither adequate language competence nor large-scale learning has a defined boundary. Successful scaling cannot establish universal necessity. These are adjudicability limits, not a broken case.

contract.note: A fundamental limit is an ordinary reading of an eventual dead end. The contract fairly requires independent verification of the antecedent and allows a decisive counterexample, while acknowledging undefined integration and success criteria.

evidence.note: The benchmark shows substantial long-context capability against a time-limited human baseline. It establishes neither general mastery nor the absence of the specified integration.
Continuing long-context hallucination problems are relevant, but present failures do not establish an eventual permanent barrier or verify the architectural antecedent.
Available before the cutoff, this study documents limited recovery from false premises. That specific failure mode cannot establish a field-wide dead end or settle the conditional forecast.

reviews.rationale: There is no deadline, the absence of the specified integration remains unverified, and no evidence meets the early-resolution rule. Benchmark progress and continuing hallucinations settle neither the eventual dead end nor the claimed necessity of integration.
